accepted.rewrite-service-page-copy.json: Metadata and one block replaced on a published service page.
accepted.publish-blog-entry.json: A new blog entry created, filled and scheduled in one set.
accepted.add-internal-link.json: An internal link into an existing canonical target, plus a full reorder.

unknown-command.json.why: A command outside the allowlist. Deleting content always needs a person, and an unknown name must fail closed rather than be ignored.

slug-in-translation-update.json.why: Moving a published address is a human-only, separately audited workflow, so the field does not exist here at all.

rationale-without-sources.json.why: A proposal with no source is an opinion presented as an analysis.

raw-html-in-block.json.why: Blocks carry data, never markup. The envelope only fixes the command shape, so this one is caught by the canonical block schema — which is the point of validating twice.

page-target-carrying-collection.json.why: One change set addresses one surface. The two publish differently, so a mixed target has no defined effect.

base-without-snapshot-hash.json.why: Without the hash there is no proof the sender read the state it claims to be changing.

reorder-repeating-a-position.json.why: An order that names a block twice has no single meaning.

contract-version-below-one.json.why: A version the server cannot map to a contract stops the change set instead of defaulting.
